title: Career Leverage: From Executor to AI-Augmented Operator
summary: Reposition career capital toward oversight, architecture, stewardship, client judgment and proof.
objectives: Map automation exposure in a role
Use AI safely in job search and career development
sections: 1. Decompose the role

A job title hides many activities. Break the role into tasks and classify routine execution, judgment, coordination, relationships, physical context, systems knowledge and authorization. Routine information transformation is usually exposed earlier than responsibilities that require context or accountability.
2. Climb the value chain

Move toward workflow ownership, preconstruction judgment, system integration, client communication, implementation, product thinking, QA, governance and change leadership. The goal is not to abandon domain expertise; it is to combine domain depth with AI fluency.
3. Build evidence

Create portfolio artifacts that show how you think: process maps, before/after workflow designs, estimating-adjacent analysis, AI opportunity audits, dashboards, QA checklists and case studies. Distinguish direct experience from transferable evidence. Never invent metrics, software expertise or scope.
4. Use agents as preparation staff

AI can scout roles, research companies, compare requirements, tailor truthful resumes, simulate interviews and maintain follow-up context. External sending, factual claims and important relationship communication remain human-approved.

title: Trading Research: AI as Scientist, Not Oracle
summary: Use AI for hypothesis formation, coding assistance, backtesting, journaling and falsification while preserving strict execution boundaries.
objectives: Turn journals into proprietary decision data
sections: 1. Keep a hard wall

AI can help formulate hypotheses, write analysis code, clean data, generate test cases, summarize journals and compare regimes. It should not generate personalized live buy/sell actions or autonomously place/modify orders. Research leverage is useful precisely because it leaves execution discipline intact.
2. Backtest scientifically

Define the rule before looking at results. Use clean data, realistic costs, correct session logic and out-of-sample testing. Separate in-sample development from walk-forward or holdout validation. Report distributions, drawdowns and failure regimes—not just average return.
3. Falsify the idea

Ask what would prove the strategy does not work. Test parameter sensitivity, neighboring markets/timeframes, different volatility regimes and delayed fills. If small changes destroy results, the strategy may be overfit.
4. Journal as proprietary data

A structured journal can capture setup, regime, planned risk, actual risk, adherence, process quality, discipline, thesis and outcome. Over time, AI can analyze patterns in your own behavior and research dataset without pretending to know the next market move.

applications.Nexus: Same measurement discipline applies to client pilots.
applications.Statecraft: Use reflection without overriding deterministic risk rules.
applications.Career: Research discipline is transferable analytical proof.
applications.Trading: Private owner track preserves strategy-specific logs and rules.

title: Physical AI, Robotics and Infrastructure Bottlenecks
summary: Understand why AI is also a robotics, energy, data-center, cooling, grid, water and construction story.
objectives: Understand infrastructure as part of AI economics
sections: 1. Physical AI moves slower

A robot must perceive, plan and act in an uncertain physical world. Failures can damage equipment or people. Dexterity, edge cases, maintenance, battery life, cost and liability slow adoption relative to pure software. Structured environments automate first.
2. Infrastructure of intelligence

AI requires chips, servers, data centers, power, cooling, networks, land, water and construction. Demand can create bottlenecks in grid interconnection, electrical equipment, skilled trades, cooling systems and permitting. These physical constraints shape where AI capacity can scale.
3. Energy and sustainability

Per-task efficiency can improve while aggregate energy use still rises because volume grows faster. Sustainable deployment depends on efficient models/hardware, clean power, scheduling, cooling, water management and grid buildout. Treat forecasts as ranges rather than certainties.
4. Opportunity lens

Look for problems created by the buildout: commissioning, maintenance, monitoring, energy optimization, cooling analytics, safety, robotics integration, construction coordination and verification. Domain knowledge about real facilities can be an edge because many AI investors understand software better than physical delivery.

applications.Nexus: Serve physical businesses with bounded automation and operational data systems.
applications.Statecraft: Teach people to position around real constraints, not just digital hype.
applications.Career: Construction/contech can intersect data-center, MEP, preconstruction and technology implementation.
applications.Trading: Infrastructure themes may inform research, but investment decisions require independent market analysis.
